facts: The Project Gutenberg eBook of "The Gambler" was authored by Fyodor Dostoyevsky.
The eBook was released on May 1, 2000.
The last update of the eBook was on July 1, 2020.
The eBook is accessible online at www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2197.
The narrator returns from a two-week leave to find the General and his family in Roulettenberg.
Polina Alexandrovna reveals that their grandmother is gravely ill.
The General warns the narrator against gambling but gives him money to play.
The narrator has a heated discussion with a Frenchman about Russian treatment abroad during the luncheon.
The narrator feels anger and discomfort as he enters the gaming rooms for the first time.
He criticizes journalists for glorifying casinos despite the reality of most players gambling small amounts.
The narrator begins to play with Polina's money and experiences unexpected luck, winning a significant amount.
He insists to Polina that he wants to gamble for himself and rejects her offer to share the winnings.
Polina avoids discussing gambling despite needing the narrator for her plans.
The General is anxious about a telegram regarding his mother.
Mlle. Blanche captures the General's affections.
Mr. Astley is infatuated with Polina but remains shy and reserved.
The narrator received 600 gülden from Polina Alexandrovna for gambling.
He initially won around 4000 gülden before losing it all.
The General and a Frenchman expressed skepticism about the narrator's gambling.
Polina Alexandrovna remained indifferent during the conversation about gambling.
The narrator has a tense conversation with Polina in the park.
Polina refers to the Marquis de Griers as a "brute."
The General is mortgaged to the Marquis, which threatens Mlle. Blanche's future.
The narrator confesses he would commit murder for Polina if she commanded it.
The narrator reflects on his impulsive behavior two days after a chaotic incident.
He fell in love with Polina after witnessing her interaction with De Griers.
The narrator was dismissed from the General's household after confronting the Baron and Baroness.
Maria Philipovna has left for Carlsbad after a dispute with the General.
The narrator has 160 gülden left.
De Griers acts as an intermediary for the General.
The narrator wants an apology from the Baron.
De Griers warns the narrator of potential police involvement.
The narrator meets Mr. Astley on the Promenade.
They go to the Casino Café for coffee.
Mlle. Blanche is linked to the General and has a questionable past.
A woman calls out for the narrator as they approach the hotel.
Antonida Vassilievna Tarassevitcha, known as the Grandmother, is seventy-five years old.
The Grandmother was presumed dead before her unexpected arrival at the General's household.
She questions the General about his finances during her visit.
The Grandmother is carried in an armchair by footmen upon her arrival.
The elderly woman is humorously registered as "Madame la générale, Princesse de Tarassevitcheva."
She wins 4,200 gülden after betting on zero at the roulette table.
Her total winnings increase to 12,000 gülden after betting on red.
She requests her winnings to be counted and placed in her purse before leaving the casino.
The Grandmother won nearly thirteen thousand florins at roulette.
She shares her winnings with her attendants and nearby beggars.
The General and De Griers are concerned about the Grandmother's gambling habits.
The narrator receives a letter for Mr. Astley from Polina.
The Grandmother becomes obsessed with gambling at the Casino.
She lost ten thousand roubles to a cunning Pole.
Alexis Ivanovitch refuses to join her in gambling again.
The Grandmother resolves to return to Moscow after her losses.
The Grandmother lost ninety thousand roubles at the Casino.
The General seeks the narrator's help due to financial ruin and rejection from Mlle. Blanche.
The Grandmother requests a loan from Mr. Astley before leaving for a train.
Polina is waiting in the darkness when the narrator returns home.
Polina presents the narrator with a letter from De Griers.
De Griers is leaving due to financial troubles.
The narrator considers Mr. Astley as a potential source of help.
The narrator wins over a hundred thousand florins at a casino.
The narrator reveals his winnings of two hundred thousand francs.
Polina reacts with contempt and refuses to accept the money.
Polina throws the money back at the narrator before leaving.
The narrator learns from a nursemaid that Polina has left the hotel.
The narrator spent a hundred thousand francs during his three-week stay in Paris.
Mlle. Blanche uses the narrator's money to fund her lavish lifestyle and parties.
Blanche prepares to marry a General while manipulating him for her benefit.
The narrator receives two thousand francs as a parting gift from Blanche.
The narrator served as a valet after being released from prison for debt.
He initially lost money at roulette but later won a significant amount.
The narrator feels disconnected from his former self and relationships, particularly with Polina.
Mr. Astley informs the narrator that Polina still cares for him.
